title: Allocating pieces to the plan

D0.outcome: Explains deciding where the main blow falls, which pieces can be spared for it, and the minimum number needed for defence.

D1.outcome: In a position with a target, names the pieces for the attack, the pieces to keep for defence, and the order of arrival.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, avoids sending every piece to the attack and keeps defenders that also serve the plan.

D3.outcome: Predicts the effect of a miscount of defenders, and mixes short-range and long-range pieces in the order of arrival.

misconceptions: All pieces should rush to the attack.
conditions: There is a definite target (the king, a weak pawn).
Defenders that also serve the centre are preferred (knight on f3 and bishop on g2).
contrasts: Reserving only the 'necessary' defenders when the count of defenders is wrong.
Short-range pieces brought in first are driven off before the plan matures.
No definite target yet, so no allocation question.

soft_prereq_notes.ATK.CASTLED.D1: piece allocation is clearest in a king attack
